newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: IMF to continue talks with Pakistan over loan.
newsitem.headline: IMF to continue talks with Pakistan over loan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will continue negotiations with Pakistan over reviving a stalled $600 million standby loan despite the sacking of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, an IMF official said on Tuesday.

"Our mission is scheduled to be here until the end of the week," the IMF's resident representative in the Pakistani capital, Shamsuddin Tareq, told Reuters. "For the time being we will continue to do work here."
Last week the IMF announced it would disburse two delayed tranches, worth about $80 million each, of the $600 million standby loan after approving Bhutto's latest economic stabilisation package.
The IMF had withheld standby loan tranches in June and September because of worries about Pakistan's budget for 1996/97 (July-June).

This week Pakistan and the IMF mission have been negotiating the terms of a commitment, called a letter of intent, which would clear the way for formal approval of the resumption of IMF lending. Resumption had been expected in late November or early December, Tareq said.

IMF director Paul Chabrier was due to arrive in Islamabad on Tuesday to try to complete the agreement. Tareq said the mission would continue its work in Islamabad despite the sacking of the government. "We have made a lot of progress," he said. "We are close to it (agreement)."
